mu_name_from: MuMain loads glove indexes 10 to 14 from GloveElf{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 151: `AccessModel(MODEL_GLOVES + i + 10, ..., L"GloveElf", i + 1)`), so index 14 is GloveElf05, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Guardian Gloves. mu.db agrees: code 5134, group 10 index 14, Player/GloveElf05.bmd.
why_this_one: The Fairy Elf's fifth and last 0.75 set, and the one Eo the Craftsman sells after Spirit - all five pieces at +3 on his shelf (src/sim/market.cpp, kCraftsman). Silver plate with gilt edging, the brightest metal in her wardrobe, and the piece that finishes his shelf.
profile_from: armour, not soft_armour. Guardian is polished silver plate with gilt edging on every sheet (upper_03, lower_03, gloves_03b, boots_03b are all grey metal at chroma about 22 with gold scroll along the edges), so plate_steel, the armour default, is what almost all of it is.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 118. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateGloves(number, name, dropLevel, defense, attackSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 5, so `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)` makes the group 10.
stats.attack_speed_note: Recorded and unread: the sim takes attack speed off the weapon row alone.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Fairy Elf alone. Eighty agility beside forty strength is the row saying the same thing in stats.

sheet_from: Data/Player/gloves_03b.OZJ (64x64), from MuMain, the only sheet the model names: one mesh, 156 triangles. The .bmd names gloves_03b.jpg.
sheet_note: gloves_03b is a silver gauntlet with gold cuff plates and gilt knuckle guards, drawn from two sides. Mean (149, 141, 125) at chroma 36.
material_note: Two islands, one gauntlet each, 78 triangles apiece on gloves_03b: plate_steel. The gold cuff plates and knuckle guards are paint on the same shell, which is the island rule; the silver is the majority by far and it is the plate.
